target_customer: Remote workers and distributed teams with many virtual meetings
problem: Calendars were built before virtual meetings; scheduling, preparing, joining and following up on meetings had friction.
business_model: Consumer and prosumer SaaS subscription for a calendar app

founders.name: Bruno Vegreville
founders.background_notes: Machine learning engineer, then product engineer and product manager per YC page.

founders.name: Louise Bayssat
founders.background_notes: Finance and customer success at a startup; community focus.

technical_complexity.rationale: A macOS calendar client on top of Google Workspace APIs is standard product engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Calendar features are easy to copy and depend on Google Calendar data; no network effects or data moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: The site announced that Hera would shut down on September 1 (year not shown); no incumbent acquisition found.

market_need_then: The 2020 to 2021 shift to remote meetings raised demand for time zone support and meeting tooling; Hera's Product Hunt launch on 2022-02-01 reached 511 upvotes and second place for the day.

branding.community_and_virality: Product Hunt 2022 launch with 511 upvotes and 221 comments; Hacker News launch post

brand_strength.rationale: A common name shared with other companies, and no press about the brand beyond launch coverage.

pivots.from: Calendar to prepare, join and follow up on virtual meetings (note taking in meetings)
pivots.to: Remote first calendar with time zone support and time protection
pivots.why: Makers say it matched their initial vision better, announced after YC

outcome_analysis: Hera raised about $2.2M from Eurazeo, Notion Capital, Kima and angels, then pivoted in September 2021 toward a remote worker calendar and did well on Product Hunt in February 2022. The company is Inactive and its website banner says it will shut down on September 1. The cause of the shutdown is not public in any source found, so failure factors stay empty.
notes: Shutdown banner on hera.so says September 1 without a year and the cause is not public; searches found no announcement. Funding databases show conflicting figures (about 1.5M EUR in one). Pre-seed date is inferred only as before the October 2021 article. No competitor sources dated near the batch were found (TechCrunch only compares to Superhuman), so the list is empty.
